name: Leveraged-ETF Close-Window Rebalance Cascade
mechanism_class: forced flow / inventory pressure (daily close-adjacent calendar flow)
economic_actor_story: Leveraged and inverse ETF issuers (TQQQ/SQQQ/SPXL/SDS complex; tens of $B AUM, largest relative to depth in NQ) must rebalance daily to hold constant leverage. The required trade is in the SAME direction as the day's move for both leveraged and inverse products (demand proportional to (L^2-L) x AUM x day-return) and is executed mechanically in the last ~30 minutes via index futures and MOC. Issuers are penalized for tracking error, not execution cost, so the flow is price-insensitive and persistent; ETF holders bear the concession, liquidity providers and front-runners collect it.
representation: Signed 09:30->15:30 ET return of NQ/ES (optionally scaled by a public (L^2-L)-weighted AUM proxy) predicts (a) continuation drift 15:30->16:00 and (b) partial reversal 16:00->next RTH open. Effect should be convex in |day return| (big-move days), and stronger in NQ than ES per LETF-AUM-to-depth ratio.
markets: NQ, ES (RTY/YM as weaker cross-checks)
data_needed: 1-min NQ/ES 2022+ only (fully satisfiable); AUM scaling is an optional $0 public refinement, plain-return version testable immediately
execution_realism: One entry ~15:30 ET at peak RTH liquidity, exit at 16:00 or next open: 1-2 crossings at NQ's measured ~3-tick RTH spread (~$15) + $4.36 commission vs documented 10-40 bp effects on large-move days - comfortably survivable. CAUTION: continuation leg overlaps the live P1 long-only intraday NQ momentum book; an orthogonality/marginal-contribution check against P1 is mandatory before any value claim.
evidence_source: Cheng & Madhavan (2009, JOIM) LETF rebalancing mechanics; Bai, Bond & Hatch (2015) late-day price impact of LETF flows; Ivanov & Lenkey (2018) LETF rebalancing and market quality; Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens (2021, JFE) 'Hedging demand and market intraday momentum' - futures-native evidence of late-day flow-driven momentum across index futures
suggested_falsifier: Regress 15:30-16:00 return on (L^2-L)-signed 09:30-15:30 return over 2022+ non-sealed windows; matched placebo = identical regression on 13:00-13:30; dependence-preserving null via circular date shift with one shared draw across NQ/ES. Kill if slope is not positive and distinct from placebo, or if the overnight reversal leg has the wrong sign.

name: Month-End Stock-Bond Rebalance Flow (Dash-for-Cash)
mechanism_class: forced flow / calendar rebalancing (month-end, quarter-end amplified)
economic_actor_story: Defined-benefit pensions, target-date funds, and sovereign allocators rebalance to fixed policy weights on a governance calendar, executing via ES/ZB futures in the final sessions of the month. After a month where equities outperform bonds they mechanically sell equity futures / buy duration (and vice versa); Etula et al. additionally document month-turn cash-need selling with post-turn reversal. Investment-policy statements fix the calendar, so the flow persists despite being publicly forecastable weeks ahead; fund beneficiaries pay the concession.
representation: Month-to-date return spread (ES minus ZB, measured through T-3) gives the sign of expected T-2..T flow in each leg. Trade WITH the flow last 2-3 sessions into month-end close, then the reversal leg T+1..T+3 of the new month. Quarter-ends and large |MTD spread| months should show amplified effects.
markets: ES/NQ/YM/RTY vs ZB/ZN (two-legged or per-leg)
data_needed: Daily 2009+ on equity index and rates roots (satisfied); 1-min 2022+ optional for entry-timing refinement
execution_realism: Multi-day holds entered at liquid RTH times; round-trip cost is a negligible fraction of the documented tens-of-bp month-end effects; no capacity concern at program size
evidence_source: Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen (2020, RFS) 'Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs'; Hartley (SSRN) on predictable end-of-month Treasury returns; widely published dealer month-end pension rebalancing estimates (Goldman/JPM) evidencing the flow is common knowledge yet persistent
suggested_falsifier: Sort 2009-2026 (pre-seal) month-ends into terciles by MTD equity-minus-bond return; test mean T-2..T and T+1..T+3 returns per leg across terciles with a circular-shift null (shared draw across the four equity roots). Require BOTH the flow leg and the reversal leg to carry the predicted signs in the extreme terciles; a flow leg without reversal, or vice versa, fails the mechanism.

name: Bond-Index Duration-Extension Day
mechanism_class: auction/fixing-adjacent forced flow (month-end index rebalancing in rates)
economic_actor_story: Passive funds tracking Bloomberg Aggregate/Treasury indices face a mechanical duration jump on the last business day of each month when new issuance enters and short/matured paper drops out. Trackers must buy duration into the month-end 15:00-16:00 ET index marks regardless of price; they are evaluated on tracking error, so the flow is inelastic and calendar-fixed. Sellers of that liquidity earn a predictable last-day rates rally; the effect scales with the month's projected index extension (issuance-heavy months).
representation: Calendar event: last business day of month, long ZB from ~14:00 ET into the 16:00 close mark, exit at/after the mark; separately test the daily version (last-day close-to-close) 2009+ and a fade leg over the first 1-2 sessions of the new month. Conditioning refinement: refunding-month vs non-refunding-month split (deterministic calendar).
markets: ZB (1-min testable), ZN via daily
data_needed: ZB 1-min 2022+ and daily 2009+ (both satisfied); no external data required - the event calendar is deterministic
execution_realism: ZB spread is typically 1 tick ($31.25) at the most liquid part of the rates day; one round trip per month against a documented single-digit-bp-of-price effect - thin but positive; the daily-horizon version is cost-trivial
evidence_source: Hartley (SSRN) 'Predictable End-of-Month Treasury Returns'; Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen (2020, RFS) document the government-bond month-turn pattern; Bloomberg index methodology (rebalancing at month-end marks) plus monthly dealer index-extension projections as the mechanism's paper trail
suggested_falsifier: Event study: mean ZB 14:00-16:00 ET return on last business days vs all other days, 2022+ intraday and 2009+ daily; circular-shift null. Decisive clause: the effect must CONCENTRATE at the close-mark window on the last day - a diffuse all-day or all-month-end-week effect indicates a different (already-known) seasonality and fails the card.

name: CL Settlement-Window TAS Hedging Pressure
mechanism_class: settlement-fixing pressure / dealer replication flow
economic_actor_story: Trade-at-Settlement (TAS) users - commodity-index rollers (USO, GSCI/BCOM trackers) and hedgers benchmarked to the daily settle - transact at the settlement price by mandate. Dealers who absorb TAS imbalance must replicate settlement by trading inside the 14:28:00-14:30:00 ET VWAP window, concentrating one-sided flow there: pre-window drift in the flow direction, post-settle reversion. Benchmark users care about tracking to settle, not level, so they keep paying; the April 20, 2020 negative-WTI episode is the mechanism's extreme realization, and CFTC v. Optiver shows it was profitably exploitable ('banging the close').
representation: 1-min CL: signed 13:30->14:25 ET drift plus abnormal volume predicts continuation into 14:28-14:30 and reversion 14:31->15:00. Condition on the deterministic amplifiers: GSCI roll window (business days 5-9), BCOM window (6-10), and the last 3 sessions before contract expiry.
markets: CL (GC excluded - no intraday data on this box)
data_needed: CL 1-min 2022+ (satisfied); roll/expiry calendars are deterministic and computable from the per-contract daily store
execution_realism: CL 1-tick spread ($10) + commission against targeted 5-20 tick moves at the single most liquid minute of the CL afternoon - marginal, must clear the house all-in cost basis explicitly; the roll-window-conditioned version has ~5 events/month, so power management matters
evidence_source: CFTC Interim Staff Report on April 20, 2020 WTI (TAS mechanics and window flow); CFTC v. Optiver (2008) enforcement - manipulation via settlement-window trading; Fernandez-Perez, Frijns et al. on the negative WTI print; fixing-pressure class evidence: Evans (FX 4pm fix), Caminschi & Heaney (2014, JFM) gold PM fix
suggested_falsifier: Event study of 14:31-15:00 return signed by the 14:00-14:28 drift, split roll-window days vs non-roll days, with an 11:00 ET same-day matched placebo window and circular-shift null. The mechanism predicts reversion concentrated on roll/expiry days; if reversion is absent there (or equally present in the placebo window), kill.

name: Commodity Index Roll-Window Congestion (post-decay re-measurement)
mechanism_class: roll-period flow / predictable rebalancing congestion
economic_actor_story: Passive commodity-index capital (GSCI- and BCOM-linked, historically >$100B) rolls long front-month positions to the next contract on a fixed public schedule (GSCI: 20% clips on business days 5-9). Trackers minimize tracking error, not roll cost, so the selling of F1 / buying of F2 is inelastic and pre-announced. Mou measured ~3%+ annual drag pre-2010 from front-running; Bessembinder et al. later showed sunshine-trading liquidity provision competed most of it away - so this card is explicitly a CONDITIONAL re-measurement: does congestion reappear when arbitrage capital is impaired (high-vol months, low spread OI, post-2020)?
representation: Per-contract daily closes: F1-F2 calendar-spread return during the roll window vs matched non-window days, unconditional first, then conditioned on vol regime and spread liquidity proxies. Expressible either as a calendar-spread position or as a roll-timing overlay (hold F2 rather than F1 through the window).
markets: CL primary; GC, SI and other index-weighted roots via the daily store
data_needed: Daily per-contract 2009+ (satisfied - this is exactly what the per-contract store enables)
execution_realism: CME calendar spreads trade at sub-outright effective cost and the horizon is days - cost-trivial; the honest risk is not cost but the documented alpha decay, hence the conditional framing
evidence_source: Mou (2011, SSRN) 'Limits to Arbitrage and Commodity Index Investment: Front-Running the Goldman Roll'; Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle & Venkataraman (2016, JFE) 'Liquidity, Resiliency and Market Quality Around Predictable Trades' (the decay evidence); Stoll & Whaley (2010) on index investing flows
suggested_falsifier: 2015+ daily panel: mean F1-F2 spread return over GSCI roll days vs circular-shifted placebo windows, then the vol/liquidity-conditioned split with its matched unconditional control in the same wave. If neither the unconditional nor any pre-specified conditional cell shows the cheapening-then-normalization signature, close as competed-away (expected outcome; cheap to run against data already owned).

name: Equity Futures Roll Richness as Liquidity-Demand Gauge
mechanism_class: roll-period flow / dealer balance-sheet inventory pricing
economic_actor_story: Asset owners who must hold equity exposure via futures (equitization mandates, leverage constraints, no cash-replication capability) roll long every quarter; dealers on the short side of the calendar spread charge balance-sheet and funding rents that vary with net positioning. The roll's richness/cheapness is therefore a directly observable PRICE of net liquidity demand. Hazelkorn-Moskowitz-Vasudevan show futures-cash basis deviations measure demand imbalance and predict both basis reversion and subsequent index returns; the long side keeps paying because mandates are fixed and the quarterly calendar is immovable.
representation: Per-contract daily store: ES/NQ calendar-spread level z-scored against its own roll-cycle seasonal (avoids needing an external rates curve), sampled through the ~2-week roll period. Two signals: (a) roll-week richness -> post-roll spread normalization; (b) basis-richness level -> multi-week outright index return tilt (rich basis = crowded long demand = lower subsequent returns, and conversely).
markets: ES, NQ, YM, RTY; construction ports to ZB/ZN rolls
data_needed: Daily per-contract 2009+ (satisfied); optional short-rate proxy if among the ~20 daily roots, but the own-seasonal z-score version needs nothing external
execution_realism: Daily-horizon positions in the most liquid contracts on CME; costs negligible relative to the documented multi-bp-per-day basis dynamics; signal (b) is a low-frequency tilt, not a trading system, and should be judged as regime input if (a) fails
evidence_source: Hazelkorn, Moskowitz & Vasudevan (2023, Journal of Finance) 'Beyond Basis Basics: Liquidity Demand and Deviations from the Law of One Price'; OFR and Fed notes on equity index futures financing richness 2016-2018; CME roll-cost analytics documenting systematic roll-period spread dynamics
suggested_falsifier: Quarterly panel 2009+: (a) regress post-roll-week spread normalization on roll-week richness z; (b) regress next-2-week outright return on basis z; circular-shift null across quarters, one shared draw across the four equity roots. Kill if neither leg shows a sign-stable slope; a leg-(b)-only result downgrades to regime-input, not engine.

name: Post-Sweep Liquidity-Provision Reversal (forced-aggressor conditioned)
mechanism_class: liquidity recovery after sweeps / market-maker inventory reversion
economic_actor_story: Forced aggressors - margin-called accounts, clustered stop-loss triggers (Osler: stops cluster at round numbers and cascade), risk-limit unwinds - demand immediacy in size at moments of their maximum weakness. The marginal supplier is a thin HFT market-making book whose inventory limits force a temporary concession beyond fundamental value; Nagel and Hendershott-Menkveld show that concession is a rentable, mean-reverting premium, and Brogaard et al. show non-fundamental extreme moves revert while news-driven ones do not. The flow persists because forced trades are by construction non-discretionary.
representation: 1-min bars: sweep event = past-m-minute return exceeding k x rolling sigma AND volume above its 95th percentile AND close beyond an n-day extreme; fade toward pre-sweep VWAP with a 30-60 min time stop; HARD exclusion of scheduled macro-release windows (calendar already in-house) as the fundamental/non-fundamental proxy. Cross-sectional consistency across the six 1-min roots is itself a gate.
markets: ES, RTY, YM, ZB, CL (NQ included but flagged: house law says NQ is the momentum outlier)
data_needed: 1-min 2022+ on all six roots (satisfied) + existing macro-release timestamps
execution_realism: Fading requires crossing an elevated-vol spread twice: at NQ's measured 3-tick RTH spread only large-k events (30-100+ tick expected reversion) survive; ES/ZB tighter. Event selection thins the path, so the house rate-matched side-blind thinning placebo is mandatory before quoting any DD-based figure.
evidence_source: Nagel (2012, RFS) 'Evaporating Liquidity'; Hendershott & Menkveld (2014, JFE) 'Price Pressures'; Brogaard, Carrion, Moyaert, Riordan, Shkilko & Sokolov (2018, JFE) 'High-Frequency Trading and Extreme Price Movements'; Kirilenko, Kyle, Samadi & Tuzun (2017, JF) Flash Crash; Osler (2003, JF) stop-loss clustering
suggested_falsifier: Event study of post-sweep 30-min drift for ex-macro sweeps vs (a) macro-window sweeps and (b) vol-matched non-sweep placebo minutes, shared-draw circular null. The mechanism predicts reversion ONLY in the ex-macro forced-flow cell. Decisive extra clause given MC-58's closed-as-generic-MR verdict: the volume+extreme conditioning must beat a plain k-sigma MR control in the same wave, else this is a rehash and dies regardless of raw significance.

name: Margin-Spiral OI-Purge Overshoot
mechanism_class: forced liquidation / margin-driven deleveraging cascade
economic_actor_story: Clearinghouse margin models (SPAN/vol-based) mechanically raise initial margin after volatility spikes; levered position holders whose margin-to-equity binds must cut regardless of view. The signature distinguishing forced liquidation from ordinary opinion transfer is POSITION DESTRUCTION: large move + vol jump + falling aggregate open interest. Brunnermeier-Pedersen formalize the spiral; Cheng-Kirilenko-Xiong document financial traders' convective risk outflows in commodity futures under stress; BIS/CPMI-IOSCO documented the March 2020 procyclical margin-call wave. The overshoot rebounds over 1-2 weeks once margin pressure clears; it persists because margin rules are mechanical and procyclical by design.
representation: Daily per-contract: liquidation-day signature = |return| > k x sigma AND realized-vol jump (proxy for margin hike, computable from daily ranges) AND aggregate-OI decline beyond threshold. Spiral continuation days 0-2, contrarian entry ~t+2, reversion horizon days 3-10. Fallback if the daily store lacks OI: vol-jump + range signature only, with an explicitly reduced claim.
markets: CL, GC, SI, ZB, ES and other daily roots (cross-sectional test)
horizon: 1-2 weeks, event-driven (roughly 5-15 events/root/decade at strict thresholds - power must be pooled cross-sectionally)
data_needed: Daily per-contract 2009+ with volume/OI fields - the ONE data check this card needs is whether OI is populated in the existing store; everything else is computable
execution_realism: Daily horizon, most liquid roots: costs negligible; the real risks are event scarcity (power) and catching genuine regime breaks - hence the old-regime-failure-is-risk-classification doctrine applies
evidence_source: Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009, RFS) 'Market Liquidity and Funding Liquidity' (margin spirals); Cheng, Kirilenko & Xiong (2015, Review of Finance) 'Convective Risk Flows in Commodity Futures Markets'; Hedegaard (2014) on commodity margin changes; BIS/CPMI-IOSCO (2022) review of March 2020 margin procyclicality
suggested_falsifier: The distinguishing prediction vs generic daily MR (which house law says is weak/absent outside NQ momentum): days 3-10 reversion must be conditional on the OI-purge signature and ABSENT in equal-|move|, equal-vol days without OI decline - that matched unconditional control runs in the same wave per house rule. Pooled cross-sectionally with one shared circular-shift draw per family. If conditioning adds nothing over the control, close as generic MR.

name: Treasury roll-window calendar drift (front-running the passive bond roll)
mechanism_class: calendar / roll-flow relative value
economic_actor_story: Passive bond funds, index ETFs, and mandate-constrained asset managers hold structural longs in ZN/ZB that they must roll every quarter before first notice day — they cannot take delivery and must track a benchmark, so their roll is concentrated in a public, calendar-predictable window (~5-10 business days pre-FND). They pay for immediacy in the calendar spread; liquidity providers who pre-position earn the concession. The flow persists because the constraint is structural (no-delivery mandates) and the dates are public.
representation: From per-contract daily settles: calendar spread S_t = P(front) - P(back). Event-time panel anchored on front's first-notice date; measure S drift over days -15..-1 per cycle; signal = hold the calendar in the direction of the documented drift from day -k to -j. Optional conditioner: open-interest migration if OI exists in the daily store.
markets: ZN, ZB (primary); analog exists in ES/NQ but that is financing-driven (separate card)
horizon: 3-10 business days, quarterly event (~68 cycles/root since 2009)
data_needed: Per-contract daily 2009+ on ZN/ZB (have); contract calendar computable from per-contract data itself
execution_realism: ZN/ZB calendars during roll month are the deepest spread markets on CME (ZN spread half-tick ~$15.6); documented drift is a few ticks, so edge must clear ~1-2 ticks RT — marginal but feasible at multi-day hold. Real risk is decay: predictable-flow concessions shrank after 2012-2016 as sunshine-trading liquidity arrived.
evidence_source: Mou (2011, SSRN) 'Limits to Arbitrage and Commodity Index Investment: Front-Running the Goldman Roll' (commodity analog, ~3.6%/yr pre-2010); Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle, Venkataraman (JFE 2016) 'Liquidity, Resiliency, and Market Quality Around Predictable Trades' (shows the concession is real but partially competed away); CME Group Treasury-roll research notes; delta-one desk roll monitors (GS/JPM).
suggested_falsifier: Event-time panel of daily calendar-spread changes across all cycles 2009+, split pre/post-2016. Gate 1: mean drift in a pre-registered window significant under a cycle-level circular-shift null. Gate 2 (different computation): sign-consistency across cycles >= 60%. Placebo: identical windows shifted +/-1 month off-cycle must show nothing.

name: Basis-momentum (Boons-Prado) on the 5 curve-bearing roots
mechanism_class: curve structure / cross-sectional ranking
economic_actor_story: Basis-momentum — the gap between the front contract's momentum and the second nearby's — spikes when curve moves are non-parallel, the signature of imbalance between hedging pressure at the front and arbitrage/financing capacity linking maturities. When the capital that normally ties maturities together is impaired, whoever supplies liquidity to the strained end earns a premium; the payer is the constrained hedger or mechanical roller who must transact at that end regardless of price. This is compensation for volatility/liquidity provision, not a repackaged carry or momentum signal.
representation: Per root with two liquid maturities: BM_t = prod(1+r_front) - prod(1+r_second) over trailing ~12 months (also test 4-12 week variant). Two expressions: (a) cross-sectional — rank CL/GC/SI/ZN/ZB, long high-BM vs short low-BM, vol-scaled; (b) within-root calendar trade — long front/short second when BM high.
markets: CL, GC, SI, ZN, ZB (equity indices excluded: their curve is pure financing)
data_needed: Per-contract daily 2009+ (have) — this is exactly the data the signal was built for
execution_realism: Monthly-turnover outrights and calendar spreads clear costs easily at this horizon. Honest weakness is breadth, not cost: 5 roots vs the paper's 21+ commodities — the cross-sectional arm is underpowered by construction; the within-root spread arm is the realistic one.
evidence_source: Boons & Prado, 'Basis-Momentum', Journal of Finance 74(1) 2019 — t-stats > 4, survives controls for basis and momentum, prices both outright and spreading returns; parent decomposition: Szymanowska, de Roon, Nijman, van den Goorbergh, 'An Anatomy of Commodity Futures Risk Premia', JF 2014 (basis predicts spreading returns).
suggested_falsifier: Compute BM 2009 -> seal boundary. Gate 1: within-root spread-expression Sharpe > 0 under cycle-block bootstrap with monotonic rank pattern. Gate 2 (the paper's core claim, cheapest kill): in a joint regression BM must NOT be subsumed by static basis + 12m momentum on our roots — if it is, close immediately.

name: DV01-neutral ZB-ZN slope carry/roll-down (preferred-habitat premium)
mechanism_class: relative value / curve
economic_actor_story: The long end of the Treasury curve is dominated by price-insensitive actors: pensions/LDI and insurers matching liabilities (they buy duration when it is expensive), Treasury issuance policy, and Fed QE/QT. None respond to expected-return signals, so the expected return of the slope position (carry + roll-down on a duration-neutral spread) is not arbitraged away. The structural payer is the liability hedger; the collector is whoever holds the slope with positive carry.
representation: Hedge ratio h_t from rolling regression of ZB on ZN daily changes (empirical DV01 ratio). Slope position = ZB - h*ZN. Carry proxy per root computed from its OWN futures calendar spread (annualized front-back, no cash curve needed); slope carry = carry_ZB - h*carry_ZN. Hold slope in the sign of slope carry, weekly rebalance.
markets: ZN, ZB (add ZF if present in the ~20 daily roots)
data_needed: Per-contract daily 2009+ (have); explicitly no cash-yield data required
execution_realism: Two liquid legs, weekly turnover; top-of-book costs are tiny relative to weekly slope vol. Comfortably survivable. The silent killer is hedge-ratio drift, not cost.
evidence_source: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen, Vrugt, 'Carry', JFE 2018 (carry predicts returns cross-section and time-series incl. Treasuries — verified via AQR summary); Brooks & Moskowitz, 'Yield Curve Premia' (SSRN 2017): carry+value on slope/fly positions across countries; theory: Vayanos & Vila (Econometrica 2021) preferred habitat; Greenwood & Vayanos (RFS 2014) supply effects.
suggested_falsifier: Sign test: does slope-carry sign predict next-week DV01-neutral spread return 2009+ under circular-shift null, with a beta-stability audit alongside. Control (kills the RV claim): if the signal's P&L reduces to level-carry on outright ZB alone, it is not a slope effect — close.

name: CL storage-state (backwardation/contango percentile) as regime conditioner
mechanism_class: curve-as-conditioner (state variable, not a signal)
economic_actor_story: Theory of storage: low inventory -> backwardation -> high convenience yield, higher spot vol, right-skewed distribution, and the Keynesian producer-hedging premium concentrates there. High inventory -> contango bounded by storage cost until capacity binds (Apr 2020), where trapped financial longs who cannot take delivery (USO-type flows) pay storage arbitrageurs to escape. The payer flips with the state, which is why an unconditional CL strategy averages two different economies.
representation: Slope_t = ln(F2/F1) * 365/days-between from per-contract dailies; state = rolling 3-yr percentile bucket {deep backwardation, mild, contango, super-contango}. Use as a GATE on any CL policy (momentum sign, MR on/off, vol sizing). Built-in placebo: the same construction on GC/SI (slope = pure rates carry) must show nothing.
markets: CL primary; GC/SI as designed negative controls
horizon: State changes over weeks; conditioned policies days-weeks
data_needed: Per-contract daily 2009+ (have)
execution_realism: A conditioner adds zero trades; conditioned strategies inherit their own cost profile. Nothing to survive at this layer.
evidence_source: Gorton, Hayashi, Rouwenhorst, 'The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns', RFS 2013 (inventory -> basis -> premia and vol); Szymanowska et al. JF 2014; Working (1949) storage theory; CFTC Interim Staff Report on April 20, 2020 negative WTI.
suggested_falsifier: Class-conditional table of CL next-week return, realized vol, and skew by slope bucket WITH the matched unconditional control in the same wave (house rule). Gate: vol/skew differ across buckets at block-bootstrap p<0.05 BEFORE any P&L claim; GC/SI must fail the same test or the 'storage' interpretation is dead.

name: Equity-index cross-sectional relative strength (compressed factor-flow momentum)
mechanism_class: cross-sectional ranking / relative value
economic_actor_story: The NQ/ES/RTY/YM cross-section is a compressed factor space (long-duration growth vs small-value cyclical). Flows chase realized factor winners with a lag (retail options and thematic creation in NQ names), while the structural counterparty is the calendar rebalancer — target-date funds, 60/40 mandates, vol-targeters — who mechanically sells relative winners into relative losers on a schedule regardless of price, financing the drift. Rebalancing flow is documented, predictable, and cannot stop (it is the mandate).
representation: Beta-neutral pairs (e.g., NQ - beta*RTY) and a 2-long/2-short rank portfolio across all four; signal = trailing 4-12 week relative-return z, weekly rebalance. Distinct second arm on 1-min 2022+ data: decompose relative strength into overnight-only vs intraday-only legs to locate which session carries the spread drift (novel representation, cheap with existing data).
markets: NQ, ES, RTY, YM
data_needed: Daily 2009+ all four (have); 1-min 2022+ (have)
execution_realism: Weekly two-leg turnover trivially clears measured NQ-class costs; RTY quotes ~1-2 ticks wide but immaterial at weekly holds.
evidence_source: Asness, Moskowitz, Pedersen, 'Value and Momentum Everywhere', JF 2013 (cross-sectional momentum in an equity-index futures universe); counterparty side: Parker, Schoar, Sun (AER 2023) on target-date-fund contrarian rebalancing flows; Etula, Rinne, Suominen, Vaittinen, 'Dash for Cash' (JFE 2020) on predictable month-end flows.
suggested_falsifier: Honesty about N first: 6 pairs are one correlated family (effective K ~ 2). Gate: pooled spread-momentum t > 2 under a shared-draw, dependence-preserving null across pairs; monotonicity across the rank portfolio as the second computation. If only one pair drives it, classify as selection luck and close.

name: SI-vs-GC relative curve tightness (physical squeeze persistence)
mechanism_class: relative value / curve divergence
economic_actor_story: GC contango is near-pure financed cost-of-carry (vault gold is abundant); SI periodically develops genuine physical tightness — COMEX-eligible stock drawdowns, EFP dislocations (Mar 2020), the Feb 2021 retail squeeze, 2024-25 lease-rate spikes. When SI's curve tightens RELATIVE to GC's (differencing cancels the common rates term), structurally short carry traders (bullion banks short futures vs OTC/physical) face rising borrow/recall cost and cover over days-to-weeks — a slow forced flow. The payer is the short carry trader caught by delivery friction.
representation: T_t = slope_SI - slope_GC, slope = annualized ln(F2/F1) per root from per-contract dailies. Signal: z(T) over rolling 1 yr; when z < -threshold (SI relatively backwardated), long SI vs beta-neutral short GC, hold to z-reversion with a time stop.
markets: SI, GC
data_needed: Per-contract daily 2009+ (have)
execution_realism: GC tight; SI ~1-2 ticks — minor at multi-week holds with vol-scaled legs. Sizing must respect SI's fat tails; episodes cluster with vol spikes.
evidence_source: Fama & French (1988) 'Business Cycles and the Behavior of Metals Prices' (metals basis/storage); BIS Bulletin and academic post-mortems of the March 2020 COMEX-London gold EFP dislocation; CFTC/press records of the Feb 2021 silver squeeze; bullion-desk EFP/lease-rate commentary.
suggested_falsifier: Event-ledger first: count z<-2 episodes 2009 -> seal (expect ~10-20). If <10, declare N-bound underpowered and close without spending — this cannot be moved with money. Otherwise: median forward beta-neutral SI-GC return vs matched unconditional windows, plus the rate-matched random-thinning placebo before quoting any DD-based figure.

name: Equity-index roll-cycle financing richness (leverage-demand premium in the calendar)
mechanism_class: calendar structure / financing relative value
economic_actor_story: The ES/NQ calendar spread embeds a financing premium dealers charge the structurally LONG futures community (leverage-constrained pensions, sovereigns, levered retail) who must buy every roll — holding cash equities is not an option for them. When dealer balance sheet is scarce (post-2014 leverage-ratio regulation, quarter-ends), the roll richens ahead of roll week and normalizes after; swings of tens of bp annualized are documented. The asset manager pays because his demand for embedded leverage is inelastic.
representation: No dividend/rate feed, so only differenced constructions are honest: (a) cycle-aligned z — current calendar spread (index-point, level-scaled) vs the SAME contract-month cycle across prior years; (b) cross-index RV — NQ-roll richness minus ES-roll richness (common financing shocks; dividend differences imperfectly cancel — flagged). Trade: short the rich calendar 2-3 weeks pre-roll, cover in roll week.
markets: ES, NQ (RTY/YM calendars thinner)
data_needed: Per-contract daily 2009+ (have). Caveat honestly stated: spread LEVEL is dividend-confounded; only the differenced representations are testable with this data.
execution_realism: ES calendar in roll month is extremely deep (0.05-pt increments, $2.50); cost negligible vs 0.5-2 index-point richness swings. Back-month is illiquid off roll-month — entries restricted to the liquid window.
evidence_source: Hazelkorn, Moskowitz, Vasudevan, 'Beyond Basis Basics: Leverage Demand and Deviations from the Law of One Price', JF 2023 — equity index futures basis as the price of leverage demand, predicts basis changes and returns; BIS Quarterly Review Dec 2017 box on the rising equity futures financing premium; Frazzini-Pedersen embedded-leverage framework; CME 'Big Roll' notes and delta-one roll monitors.
suggested_falsifier: Panel of cycle-aligned calendar paths 2009+ (~68 cycles/root). Gate 1: pre-registered richen-then-cheapen shape significant under cycle-level permutation, stable post-2016. Gate 2 (different computation, from Hazelkorn et al.): richness must co-move across ES and NQ within cycle — if the two indices' richness is uncorrelated, the financing interpretation fails.

name: Gold/silver beta-residual overshoot unwind (spec-amplification, NOT cointegration)
mechanism_class: relative value (cross-metal residual reversion)
economic_actor_story: Silver futures carry the highest small-speculator/retail share of major metals; gold's flow is institutional. After large common shocks, SI overshoots its gold beta because spec positioning piles in with the move and later unwinds into thin liquidity. The loser is the late trend-follower/retail momentum trader in SI; the collector is the liquidity-providing fader. Explicitly NOT the classic ratio-level trade — the long-run GC/SI cointegration broke decades ago and that version is the known failure mode.
representation: Rolling 60-day beta of SI on GC returns; residual e_t = r_SI - beta*r_GC cumulated over 5-15 days; fade cumulated-residual extremes (|z|>2) with a beta-neutral pair and a 2-4 week time stop. COT small-spec positioning as an optional free enhancer (unprobed surface per campaign notes).
markets: GC, SI
data_needed: Daily 2009+ (have); COT free/optional
execution_realism: Same cost profile as the SI/GC curve card; fine at horizon. Overshoot events cluster with vol — size on vol, not fixed notional.
evidence_source: Ciner (2001, Global Finance Journal) — GC/SI cointegration broke (warning against the naive ratio version); Erb & Harvey (FAJ 2006) on metals ratio instability; the card's actual economics: Kang, Rouwenhorst, Tang, 'A Tale of Two Premiums: The Role of Hedgers and Speculators in Commodity Futures Markets', JF 2020 — short-horizon reversal premium earned by liquidity providers against impatient speculative flow.
suggested_falsifier: Residual-overshoot event study 2009+ with matched unconditional control and the house rate-matched random-thinning placebo. Decisive kill given the campaign's law that 'everything mean-reverts': run the identical construction on a placebo pair with no spec-share asymmetry (e.g., GC-vs-ZB beta residual) — if the placebo shows the same edge, this is generic MR, not a mechanism; close it.

name: London-Handoff Overnight Drift
mechanism_class: session transfer / overnight-vs-intraday decomposition
economic_actor_story: US dealers and market-makers end the RTH session with inventory imbalances forced on them by close-auction and late-afternoon liquidity demanders (derisking institutions, MOC flow). They cannot lay off risk in the thin Asia tape and pay for immediacy when the first deep liquidity pool arrives at the European open. After down US days the imbalance is short-side, so buy-back demand at London open produces a positive drift concentrated around 02:00-03:00 ET; the flow persists because end-of-day risk limits and the closing-auction hedging cycle are structural, and the payers (immediacy demanders at the US close) are mandate-bound.
representation: Event-relative to London open (08:00 London, DST-aware, i.e. 02:00 or 03:00 ET): average return path from 60 min before to 60 min after London open, conditioned on sign/size of the prior US RTH open-to-close return. Trade form: long index futures across the London-open window, sized up after negative prior RTH days. Companion decomposition: split close(16:00 ET)->open(09:30 ET) into Asia leg (18:00-02:00 ET) vs Europe leg (02:00-09:30 ET) and attribute the overnight premium.
markets: NQ, ES, RTY, YM (ZB as non-equity control)
data_needed: 1-min bars 2022+ on NQ/ES/RTY/YM/ZB (available); DST-aware London-clock mapping; measured NQ cost data for net figures. No new data.
execution_realism: Two crossings of the overnight spread at 02:00-03:00 ET, a moderate-liquidity (European) window - wider than RTH, thinner book. Documented gross effect is bp-scale per hour, so survivability is THE open question: must clear the measured NQ ALL_IN overnight cost; ES (1-tick, deep) is the more survivable venue. One RT/day caps friction.
evidence_source: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan, 'The Overnight Drift', NY Fed Staff Report 917 (verified via newyorkfed.org fetch 2026-09-06: drift concentrated in early European hours, dealer-inventory mechanism, robust positive overnight reversal after declines, modest after rallies); Lou, Polk & Skouras, 'A Tug of War: Overnight vs Intraday Expected Returns', JFE 2019.
suggested_falsifier: On 1-min ES/NQ 2022-01 -> 2026-05 (pre-burn), compute the event-relative mean return curve around London open with a circular-shift null and a matched placebo window (same duration, randomly drawn Globex hour, shared draw across the family). Kill if the 02:00-03:00 window mean, net of measured ALL_IN overnight cost, is not distinguishable from the placebo, or if the prior-day-sign conditioning does not replicate the documented asymmetry (strong after down days, weak after up days).

name: Close-Auction Hedging Cascade
mechanism_class: intraday seasonality interaction (end-of-day hedging-demand momentum)
economic_actor_story: Leveraged/inverse ETF issuers must rebalance in the direction of the day's move near the cash close (daily-reset mandate), and short-gamma option dealers hedge in-trend into the close. Both are price-insensitive and time-fixed, so they pay whoever is positioned with the day's move in the last half hour. The flow persists because the products' daily reset and dealer risk limits are contractual/structural, and its size scales with the day's amplitude and the outstanding gamma imbalance - which makes it an interaction, not a fixed clock bucket.
representation: Sign of RTH day-so-far return (09:30 -> 15:30 ET; also first-half-hour 09:30-10:00 as separate predictor per Gao et al.) -> same-sign position 15:30 -> 16:00 ET, exit at RTH close. Interaction terms: |day-so-far move|, trailing realized vol, OPEX-week dummy. Prediction: slope positive, monotone in amplitude, strongest on high-vol and expiry-adjacent days.
markets: NQ, ES, RTY, YM
data_needed: 1-min bars 2022+ (available); measured NQ costs. No new data.
execution_realism: Best liquidity of the day (pre-close); one RT/day at RTH-tight spreads. Documented gross effect is a few bp per day - clears measured NQ RTH costs only if the conditional (high-amplitude) subset is used; unconditional version likely marginal.
evidence_source: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou, 'Market Intraday Momentum', JFE 2018 (first half-hour predicts last half-hour); Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens, 'Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum', JFE 2021 (effect present across 16 international index futures, driven by leveraged-ETF and option-hedging demand). Citations from scout knowledge; not re-verified this session (search budget exhausted).
suggested_falsifier: Regress last-30-min return on open-to-15:30 return per instrument, 2022 -> 2026-05, yearly subsamples. Require positive slope stable across years AND failure of a placebo family (random mid-day 30-min terminal windows, shared draw). Then net-of-cost sign-strategy through eval_battery with rate-matched thinning placebo. Kill if the slope lives only in 2022 (the known high-vol year) or only in the unconditional bucket already closed by prior clock-bucket work.

name: Tug-of-War Component Persistence
mechanism_class: overnight-vs-intraday return decomposition
economic_actor_story: Distinct clienteles transact at the open vs the close (retail and mutual-fund flow concentrates at/near the open; institutional rebalancing at the close), so the overnight and intraday return components are driven by different persistent demand processes: each component exhibits own-component momentum and cross-component reversal. The losers are clienteles that demand liquidity at their mandated time-of-day regardless of price; the split persists because fund dealing cutoffs, margin rules, and overnight risk aversion are institutional, not informational.
representation: Decompose per-contract daily bars into overnight leg (prior close -> open) and intraday leg (open -> close) for each root, 2009+. Signal: trailing k-day sum of the overnight component (k ~ 20-60) predicts the NEXT overnight component positively; trailing intraday component predicts overnight negatively. Trade only the predicted leg (enter near close, exit near open, or vice versa). 1-min data 2022+ pins the exact session split; daily 2009+ extends history with a vendor-open-definition caveat that must be resolved first (Globex 18:00 reopen vs RTH open).
markets: All ~20 daily roots: equity idx, GC, SI, CL, ZB, ZN, 6E - cross-root breadth is the point
horizon: Hold one session leg (hours), signal horizon weeks; low turnover variant re-signs weekly
data_needed: Daily per-contract OHLC 2009+ (available) + 1-min 2022+ for session-split precision and cost realism. No new data.
execution_realism: Entries/exits near close and open, both liquid; worst case 2 RT/day, weekly-resign variant far less. Component-level daily moves are large relative to costs; the danger is not cost but that the stock-level effect may be absent at index level.
evidence_source: Lou, Polk & Skouras, JFE 2019 (tug of war, component persistence); Bogousslavsky, 'The Cross-Section of Intraday and Overnight Returns', JFE 2021; overnight-premium literature generally. Citations from scout knowledge; not re-verified this session.
suggested_falsifier: On daily data 2009 -> 2026-05: per root, corr(trailing overnight-component sum, next overnight component) with circular-shift nulls and effective-K family correction across the ~20 roots. Cheap and decisive: kill if index-futures overnight components show no own-persistence (the published effect is largely cross-sectional in single names and may not survive aggregation).

name: Month-End Dash-for-Cash
mechanism_class: calendar-flow seasonality, event-relative in trading days (turn-of-month)
economic_actor_story: Institutions facing month-end payment and redemption cycles (pensions paying benefits, funds meeting redemptions) sell equities over the last ~3 trading days of the month and the market rebounds over the first days of the next; separately, balanced mandates rebalance stock-vs-bond at month-end after large intra-month divergence, pushing flow into the underperformer. The payers persist because payment dates and rebalancing calendars are fixed, public, and mandate-bound - the flow cannot wait for better prices.
representation: Event time = trading days to month-end (T-5 ... T+3). Three constructions: (a) unconditional turn-of-month long equity T-1 close -> T+3 close; (b) conditional cross-asset: when |month-to-date ES minus ZB return gap| exceeds a threshold, position for convergence (long underperformer, short outperformer) over the last 2 sessions of the month; (c) reversal: weakness accumulated T-3..T-1 predicts T+1..T+3 rebound.
markets: ES/NQ/YM/RTY vs ZB/ZN
data_needed: Daily bars 2009+ (available). No new data.
execution_realism: Daily-scale moves dwarf spread+commission; trivially survivable. Capacity and cost are non-issues; the risk is pure signal decay.
evidence_source: Etula, Rinne, Suominen & Vaittinen, 'Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs', Journal of Finance 2020; McConnell & Xu, 'Equity Returns at the Turn of the Month', FAJ 2008; sell-side month-end pension-rebalancing estimate notes (GS/JPM flow research). Citations from scout knowledge; not re-verified this session.
suggested_falsifier: Event study by trading-day-to-month-end on daily 2009 -> 2026-05 with a null that circularly shifts whole months (preserving within-month dependence). Kill the unconditional TOM if the post-2015 subsample is flat (known decay risk); kill the conditional stock-bond version if the convergence effect is not monotone in the divergence-gap size.

name: Treasury Roll-Window Congestion
mechanism_class: roll/contract mechanics (roll-date flows)
economic_actor_story: Real-money asset managers are structurally long Treasury futures (the levered basis trade is the other side) and MUST exit the front contract before first notice day - delivery is unacceptable for an unlevered fund. Their concentrated front-selling/back-buying over a known ~5-10 day window moves the calendar spread along a predictable path; liquidity providers who pre-position earn the concession, and late rollers pay it. Persists because delivery risk is absolute, the roll window is institutionalized (CME publishes 'Pace of the Roll'), and the long base is mandate-driven.
representation: Event time = business days to first notice day of the front contract, per quarterly cycle. From per-contract daily closes, build the front-minus-back calendar spread path T-15 -> T0 and its era-stability. Signals: (a) hold the calendar spread against the documented drift through the peak-roll days; (b) outright front-contract pressure on peak-roll days as a directional overlay; (c) as pure policy alpha, time one's own hypothetical roll to the cheap side of the window.
markets: ZB, ZN (ES quarterly and CL monthly rolls as comparison controls)
horizon: 3-10 days per quarterly cycle, ~70 events since 2009
data_needed: Daily per-contract closes 2009+ (available - curve is computable); ZB 1-min 2022+ refines intraday timing. No new data.
execution_realism: Calendar spread = 2 legs but exchange-traded as a spread with minimal tick cost in ZN/ZB; daily horizon means costs are small relative to typical roll-window spread drift. Validation can proceed on close-to-close marks before any execution question.
evidence_source: CME Group 'Pace of the Roll' research/analytics; Barth & Kahn, 'Hedge Funds and the Treasury Cash-Futures Disconnect', OFR Working Paper 21-01 (documents the structural asset-manager long base); Hazelkorn, Moskowitz & Vasudevan, 'Beyond Basis Basics: Liquidity Demand and Deviations from the Law of One Price', Journal of Finance 2023 (demand-driven calendar-spread/basis deviations predict returns). Citations from scout knowledge; not re-verified this session.
suggested_falsifier: Pin the event-relative calendar-spread drift by days-to-first-notice across all quarterly rolls 2009 -> 2026-05; null = equal-length windows away from the roll, circularly shifted. Kill if mean drift < 2x spread-trading cost, if the sign flips across eras (pre/post 2015, pre/post 2020 basis-trade growth), or if the drift is fully explained by carry/repo mechanics rather than flow timing.

name: Goldman-Roll Residue in CL
mechanism_class: roll/contract mechanics (index roll-date flows)
economic_actor_story: Commodity index trackers (GSCI/BCOM mandates) and USO roll front WTI on published schedules (GSCI: business days 5-9 of the month), price-insensitively and pre-announced. Historically front-running this flow paid; post-2010 sunshine-trading attracted liquidity supply and the naive edge decayed. The card's purpose is to MEASURE the current residue - who wins now is an empirical question with an honest prior near zero, and a clean negative retires an entire folklore family cheaply.
representation: Event time = business day of month relative to the GSCI roll window (BD5-BD9). Track CL1-CL2 spread change inside vs outside the window, monthly, 2009+ (~200 events). Signal (if residue exists): enter the calendar spread before BD5 in the direction of index-roll pressure (sell front/buy back side), exit by BD9. Era-split is mandatory (2009-14 / 2015-19 / 2020-26) since index AUM and curve shape regimes changed.
markets: CL (ZB as non-commodity control; GC secondary since it also sits in the indices)
data_needed: Daily per-contract CL closes 2009+ (available); CL 1-min 2022+ for refinement. No new data.
execution_realism: CL calendar spread is among the most liquid spread markets, 1-tick wide; monthly low-turnover. Any residue that fails to clear this minimal cost is definitively dead.
evidence_source: Mou (2011), 'Limits to Arbitrage and Commodity Index Investment: Front-Running the Goldman Roll' (working paper); Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle & Venkataraman, 'Liquidity, Resiliency and Market Quality around Predictable Trades', JFE 2016 (USO roll: sunshine trading drew liquidity provision, little predation - the honest decay prior). Citations from scout knowledge; not re-verified this session.
suggested_falsifier: Diff-in-diff of CL1-CL2 spread drift inside vs outside the BD5-BD9 window by era, 2009 -> 2026-05, with month-block circular-shift nulls. Kill if the post-2015 residue is within costs (expected outcome) - and record the closure as a permanent folklore retirement either way; promote only if a powered post-2015 residue survives.

name: Witching-Week Hedge Unwind
mechanism_class: expiry effects / intraday seasonality interaction (triple witching, OPEX)
economic_actor_story: As quarterly index options and futures expire, the delta hedges backing expiring open interest are mechanically unwound, and time-decay (charm) forces hedgers of in-the-money structures to trade on an expiry-fixed schedule regardless of price. This produces pre-expiry pinning/drift during expiration week and a release/reversal after the Friday 09:30 ET SOQ settlement. The payers are hedgers rebalancing on a calendar they cannot move; the expiration calendar and hedge mandates persist by construction.
representation: Two event clocks: (a) expiration-week effect - Mon-Thu of the week containing monthly OPEX/quarterly triple witching, long-bias vs matched non-expiry weeks, on daily data (~200 monthly events 2009+); (b) SOQ-relative intraday - on quarterly witching Fridays, measure the 09:30 -> 12:00 ET move against the prior 24h pre-SOQ move (reversal hypothesis), plus the volume/range signature at the SOQ minute, on 1-min data (~19 quarterly + ~57 monthly events 2022+, pooled across ES/NQ/RTY/YM with dependence-preserving nulls).
markets: ES, NQ primary; RTY, YM pooled for power
data_needed: Daily 2009+ for the week-level effect; 1-min 2022+ for the SOQ leg; expiry calendar is deterministic (third Fridays) - constructible, no purchase. No options-surface data needed because the representation is price/calendar-only.
execution_realism: All trading in RTH at high-liquidity times; week-level version is cost-trivial, SOQ version is one RT on the busiest morning of the quarter - fine. Real risk is small N on the intraday leg, not cost.
evidence_source: Option-expiration-week effect: Stivers & Sun (JFQA) and follow-ups documenting elevated large-cap returns in expiration weeks (citation from scout knowledge - verify exact reference before preregistration); practitioner charm/vanna-flow literature (Nomura McElligott notes, SqueezeMetrics); CME/Cboe SOQ settlement mechanics documentation.
suggested_falsifier: Stage 1 (cheap, high-N): daily-data expiration-week mean vs matched-week control 2009 -> 2026-05 with week-block shifts - kill the whole card if flat. Stage 2 only on pass: pooled SOQ-relative intraday event study with one shared draw per event across the 4 instruments (family K corrected). Never run stage 2 first - the intraday leg alone is underpowered (~19 quarterly events) and would produce an unfalsifiable maybe.

name: Pre-Holiday Inventory Trim
mechanism_class: weekend/holiday effects
economic_actor_story: Ahead of exchange-holiday closures, market makers cannot hedge over the gap and shorts face unhedgeable event risk, so both trim exposure into the last pre-holiday session: short-covering demand plus withdrawn liquidity supply tilts the tape up. Documented directly in futures (not just cash equities). The payers are shorts flattening at any price and liquidity demanders in a thinning book; the mechanism persists because the holiday calendar and overnight-gap risk are structural, though modern magnitude is an open question.
representation: Event = last full trading session before a CME full closure (separately: half-days, and 3-day-weekend holidays vs midweek holidays). Constructions: (a) daily - long prior-close -> pre-holiday close vs all-ordinary-weekday control, 2009+ (~150 events); (b) intraday - 12:00 ET -> close drift on pre-holiday sessions on 1-min 2022+; (c) modern weekend analog as a secondary read: Friday 15:00-16:00 derisking vs Monday-reopen behavior.
markets: ES, NQ primary; ZB, CL, GC for the cross-asset consistency check the story implies (gap risk is universal)
data_needed: Daily 2009+ plus the CME holiday calendar - reconstructible from missing sessions in the data itself, no purchase; 1-min 2022+ for the intraday leg.
execution_realism: Daily-scale, entered in normal liquidity the day before; cost-trivial. Thin pre-holiday tape argues for entering early in the session, not at the close.
evidence_source: Ariel, 'High Stock Returns before Holidays', JF 1990; Fabozzi, Ma & Briley, 'Holiday Trading in Futures Markets', JF 1994 (futures-native evidence); day-of-week/calendar-anomaly decay literature as the honest prior that the effect may be arbitraged away. Citations from scout knowledge; not re-verified this session.
suggested_falsifier: Event study 2009 -> 2026-05: pre-holiday session mean vs all-weekday mean with a block bootstrap preserving vol clustering, era-split at 2015. Kill if the post-2015 mean is inside the control band, if 1-2 outlier events carry the entire effect, or if the cross-asset check fails (the gap-risk story predicts the same sign in ZB/GC - an equity-only result would indicate a different, weaker mechanism).

name: Compression-Primed Stop Cascade Breakout
mechanism_class: volatility transition (compression->expansion) x pre-event trend state
economic_actor_story: During multi-day range compression, protective stops from retail and risk-managed discretionary traders accumulate just outside the consolidation boundary (Osler shows on real order data that stops cluster at salient levels and execute in cascades), while dealers/CTAs cut size as realized vol falls, thinning the book at the boundary. A range break fires clustered stops into a thin book, producing follow-through beyond fair value. The losing flow persists because stop placement is insurance, not alpha. The asymmetry direction is set by which side the prior trend left more trapped positioning on: with-trend breaks should continue, counter-trend breaks fade.
representation: Compression event = trailing 5-10 day high-low range (or daily Parkinson vol) in bottom decile of its trailing 1-2yr distribution; trigger = close beyond the compression-range boundary; second state = sign of the 20-60 day prior trend; tested object is the with-trend vs against-trend split of post-break continuation, not the raw breakout.
markets: ES, NQ, CL, ZN/ZB, GC daily; intraday analog on ES/NQ/CL/ZB
data_needed: Daily bars 2009+ (range percentile, trend state); 1-min bars 2022+ for the intraday variant. Nothing new.
execution_realism: Sparse events (~1-2/month/market); one taker entry at the break. Daily-horizon variant trivially survives costs; intraday variant must clear 1 spread + fast-bar slippage, boundable with the measured NQ cost data.
evidence_source: Osler (2003, Journal of Finance, 'Currency Orders and Exchange Rate Dynamics') — stop clustering and cascade execution on dealer order data; Toby Crabel (1990) NR7/inside-day opening-range breakout; practitioner Bollinger-squeeze literature.
suggested_falsifier: Event study of all range-break events, daily 2009-2021: k-day post-break return split with-trend vs against-trend, plus a matched unconditional control (same breaks without the compression filter) in the same wave, circular-shift null. Kill if the with/against asymmetry is unpowered or the control shows the same drift.

name: Slow-Capital Post-FOMC Drift in Bond Futures
mechanism_class: macro reaction path (post-announcement drift, after the first response)
economic_actor_story: After a hawkish surprise, retail bond mutual-fund investors redeem gradually over days-weeks; funds sell into the decline; arbitrageurs demand compensation to absorb the incremental supply, so longer yields keep drifting in the announcement direction (Brooks-Katz-Lustig). The counterparty is the slow redeemer selling after the move; the flow persists because redemption is decision-lagged retail behavior with structural frictions (NAV timing, advice cycles).
representation: Event = FOMC decision days (public calendar). Surprise proxy = ZN/ZB return in the 13:55-14:30 ET window (1-min, 2022+) or announcement-day close-to-close (daily, 2009+). Position = same direction as the first response, held 1-15 business days, scaled by the announcement-window move.
markets: ZB, ZN primary; secondary read-through checks in 6E and ES
data_needed: Per-contract daily 2009+; 1-min ZB 2022+ for the window proxy; free FOMC calendar.
execution_realism: 8 events/yr, one RT each at day horizon — cost negligible vs typical multi-day ZB moves.
evidence_source: Brooks, Katz, Lustig, 'Post-FOMC Announcement Drift in U.S. Bond Markets' (NBER WP 25127, https://www.nber.org/papers/w25127 — abstract verified this session: drift in the same direction as the announcement-day move, driven by gradual mutual-fund outflows); related: Neuhierl & Weber, 'Monetary Momentum' (equity drift ~15 days after policy surprises).
suggested_falsifier: Sign-conditioned event study over ~120 FOMC days 2009-2021 daily: mean k-day drift conditional on announcement-day sign vs matched non-FOMC control days, circular-shift null; mandatory ZLB-era vs hiking-era subsample split, since the documented mechanism (redemptions) is hike-specific.

name: Jump Taxonomy: News Jumps Continue, Orphan Jumps Revert
mechanism_class: event-conditioned continuation AND event-conditioned reversal (one conditional split)
economic_actor_story: A jump coinciding with a scheduled release is price discovery: heterogeneous processing speeds mean slower traders keep pushing the jump direction for tens of minutes (Jiang-Lo-Verdelhan show announcement jumps in Treasuries carry information). A jump with no scheduled news is typically a liquidity hole or forced flow: the aggressor paid for immediacy and the concession decays as liquidity refills. Losers: slow updaters fading news jumps; forced traders paying impact on orphan jumps. Both persist structurally — information-processing speed is heterogeneous and forced liquidation is margin/mandate-driven.
representation: Jump = 1-min |return| > k x local bipower/realized vol (Lee-Mykland style). Flag = within +/-3 min of a scheduled release (FOMC/CPI/NFP/EIA/Treasury auctions; free calendars). Flagged: follow jump direction 30-120 min. Unflagged: fade over 15-60 min. The tested object is the flagged-vs-unflagged DIFFERENCE in post-jump drift.
markets: ZB, ES, NQ, CL
data_needed: 1-min bars 2022+ and free release calendars only.
execution_realism: Fade leg can rest maker-style limits; follow leg pays taker once into elevated vol where jump sizes are many multiples of the spread by construction. NQ measured costs bound the worst case.
evidence_source: Jiang, Lo, Verdelhan (JFQA 2011, 'Information Shocks, Liquidity Shocks, Jumps, and Price Discovery: Evidence from the U.S. Treasury Market'); Andersen, Bollerslev, Diebold, Vega (AER 2003; J. Int'l Economics 2007); Bjursell, Gentle, Wang (jumps around EIA releases in energy futures); Nagel (RFS 2012) for the liquidity-reversal leg.
suggested_falsifier: One event study 2022-2025: all detected jumps, 2-way table of post-jump 60-min drift flagged vs unflagged, against a matched control of same-magnitude non-jump moves; one shared draw per session across the family. Kill if the flagged/unflagged difference is unpowered.

name: EIA Inventory Reaction Ride, Curve-Gated
mechanism_class: event-conditioned continuation x pre-event curve state (interaction card)
economic_actor_story: The Wednesday 10:30 ET EIA petroleum report reprices storage economics. HFTs set the first seconds; the following 30-90 minutes carries continued same-direction flow from commercial hedgers on inelastic compliance schedules and slower discretionary funds mapping barrels into deferred months. The pre-event curve state gates informativeness: a bullish draw in backwardation (tight physical market) means more than the same draw in deep contango. Losers: mechanically slow hedge adjusters and retail fading the move; persists because hedging is scheduled, not alpha-timed.
representation: Event = EIA release timestamps (holiday-shifted Wednesdays 10:30 ET, free calendar). Surprise proxy = signed first-5-min CL return (no consensus data needed). Second state = sign/magnitude of front-second calendar spread from daily per-contract closes. Position = first-response direction, minutes 5 through 90, with the contango/backwardation split as the tested interaction.
markets: CL
data_needed: CL 1-min 2022+; per-contract daily 2009+ for the calendar spread; free EIA calendar.
execution_realism: CL spread typically 1 tick ($10); post-EIA 60-min moves routinely run 30-100+ ticks; one taker RT per event survives easily if any continuation exists.
evidence_source: Halova, Kurov, Kucher (Journal of Futures Markets, energy inventory announcements); Bu (2014, J. Futures Markets, EIA surprises and crude futures); Bjursell, Gentle, Wang (2015, jumps around inventory news in energy futures); Rousse & Sevi (informed pre-EIA positioning); Kurov, Sancetta, Strasser, Wolfe (JFQA 2019) include energy releases in pre-announcement-drift evidence.
suggested_falsifier: 2x2 table (first-response sign x curve state) of the 5-to-90-min continuation over ~190 events 2022-2025, with a matched 10:30 non-release-day control in the same wave. Kill if continuation is absent unconditionally AND the curve interaction is unpowered.

name: Trapped Pre-Positioning: Confirm vs Contradict
mechanism_class: macro reaction path x pre-event drift state (interaction card)
economic_actor_story: Kurov-Sancetta-Strasser-Wolfe document systematic drift in the direction of the coming surprise ~30 min before major US releases (leakage/early processing). When the first response CONFIRMS the pre-drift, the informed are already positioned and little flow remains. When it CONTRADICTS, the pre-positioned crowd is trapped and unwinds through stops, fueling the new direction — continuation should be conditionally stronger after contradiction. Losers: leak-followers on their bad days; the flow keeps returning because pre-positioning is profitable on average.
representation: Pre-state = signed 60-min return before release (CPI/NFP 08:30, ISM 10:00, FOMC 14:00). First response = signed 2-min release-window return. Condition = agree/disagree between the two signs. Measure continuation of the first response over the next 30-240 min, disagree cell vs agree cell.
markets: ZB (strongest in the literature), ES, NQ
data_needed: 1-min bars 2022+ and free release calendars; ~130-160 events available 2022-2025.
execution_realism: Sparse high-vol windows; taker entry after the 2-min window; release-window moves in ZB/ES are large multiples of spread.
evidence_source: Kurov, Sancetta, Strasser, Wolfe (JFQA 2019, 'Price Drift Before U.S. Macroeconomic News: Private Information about Public Announcements?'); Bernile, Hu, Tang (JFE 2016, pre-FOMC informed trading); Lucca & Moench (pre-FOMC drift) for existence of the pre-state.
suggested_falsifier: 2x2 agree/disagree x post-window drift with a matched unconditional control (same clock times on non-release days). N is borderline, so pre-commit a minimum-effect gate; kill if disagree-cell continuation is not greater than agree-cell.

name: Close-Hour Hedging-Flow Momentum, Vol-Gated
mechanism_class: event-conditioned continuation (intraday vol-expansion event -> mechanical close flow)
economic_actor_story: Leveraged/inverse ETF issuers must rebalance in the direction of the day's move near the close, and short-gamma option dealers hedge the same way; both flows are mechanical, same-direction, and scale with the day's realized move. Baltussen-Da-Lammers-Martens tie market intraday momentum in index futures directly to these hedging demands and show concentration on high-vol days. The losers are the issuers/dealers themselves paying the impact — they persist because mandates (tracking error, risk limits) force the trade regardless of price.
representation: Signal = sign of session return from prior close (alternately from the first 30 min) measured at ~15:00 ET. Gate = day's realized move relative to trailing RV in top tercile (the vol event). Position = same direction, 15:00 to 16:00 ET, flat at the cash close. The gate x signal interaction is the tested object.
markets: ES primary (deepest evidence), RTY, YM; NQ deliberately excluded (overlaps the live P1 long-only intraday momentum book)
horizon: 30-60 minutes, at most once per qualifying day
data_needed: 1-min ES/RTY/YM 2022+ only.
execution_realism: One RT/day at the most liquid hour of the day; source papers document the effect net of realistic ES costs, and the vol gate raises per-trade gross precisely where costs are paid.
evidence_source: Gao, Han, Li, Zhou (JFE 2018, 'Market Intraday Momentum'); Baltussen, Da, Lammers, Martens (JFE 2021, 'Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum') — futures evidence in ES and international index futures, extensions to bonds and energy.
suggested_falsifier: Conditional table of last-hour return by sign of day-to-15:00 return x vol-gate state, with the matched ungated control in the same wave, circular-shift null, AND the rate-matched side-blind random-thinning placebo (the gate thins samples, so repo law requires it).

name: Stress-Time Liquidity Provision Reversal
mechanism_class: volatility transition (expansion state) -> short-horizon event-conditioned reversal
economic_actor_story: When RV expands, market makers cut inventory limits and widen; transient price impact per unit flow rises. Anyone forced to trade immediately in that state (margin calls, de-grossing, stop cascades) pays a temporarily inflated concession that decays. Nagel shows short-term-reversal PnL is compensation for liquidity provision and scales with vol. Losers: forced de-riskers; the flow persists because margin and mandate constraints bind exactly in stress. House cross-asset law (everything but NQ mean-reverts) is independently consistent with this card.
representation: Vol event = trailing 3-5 day RV in top quintile OR intraday RV >= 2x prior day. Signal = z-scored 15-60-min return vs session VWAP. Position = fade beyond a z-threshold, maker-style entries, exit on mean-touch or 2-4 hr time stop. Strategy exists ONLY inside the vol-expansion state; the high-vol minus low-vol PnL difference is the tested object.
markets: ES, ZN/ZB, CL (not NQ: momentum outlier per house law, and correlation hygiene vs live P1)
data_needed: 1-min bars 2022+; measured NQ BBO/costs only as a worst-case cost bound.
execution_realism: The hard card: short-horizon MR is cost-dominated in calm regimes — which is the mechanism's own prediction. Only the gated version can clear spread; must be evaluated at ALL_IN cost basis with maker-fill haircuts, per repo cost law.
evidence_source: Nagel (RFS 2012, 'Evaporating Liquidity'); Grossman & Miller (1988) market-making framework; Khandani & Lo (2007 quant unwind) as the canonical forced-flow episode.
suggested_falsifier: Compute fade-PnL in top vs bottom vol quintile 2022-2025; gates: (1) high-minus-low gross difference powered, (2) high-vol net > 0 at ALL_IN basis; random-thinning placebo mandatory since the state gate removes trades.

name: Delayed Overshooting: FX Drift After Monetary Surprises
mechanism_class: macro reaction path (weeks-scale post-announcement drift in FX after the first response)
economic_actor_story: Dornbusch predicts immediate overshoot then reversion after a monetary surprise; Eichenbaum-Evans showed the dollar instead keeps appreciating for weeks-months after a tightening surprise (delayed overshooting). Micro story: FX flow is dominated by corporates and real money that adjust hedge ratios on quarterly committee schedules, plus carry capital that ramps in only as the rate differential materializes meeting by meeting. Losers: slow hedge adjusters and early textbook-reversion faders; persists because hedging policy is governance-constrained, not price-responsive.
representation: Event = FOMC days (optionally ECB). Surprise proxy = event-day ZN close-to-close return (sign of the rate surprise) or event-day 6E return. Position = 6E in the surprise direction (hawkish Fed -> short 6E), held 5-20 business days, re-set per meeting. Carry must be residualized out so this is not rebadged carry.
markets: 6E daily (per-contract, so the carry control is computable in-house)
data_needed: Daily 6E and ZN 2009+ per-contract; free FOMC/ECB calendars. Fully satisfiable.
execution_realism: 8-16 RT/yr at weekly horizon — friction irrelevant.
evidence_source: Eichenbaum & Evans (QJE 1995, 'Some Empirical Evidence on the Effects of Shocks to Monetary Policy on Exchange Rates'); Scholl & Uhlig (2008) — the effect is identification- and sample-sensitive, which the falsifier must respect; Brooks-Katz-Lustig (NBER WP 25127) for the same slow-capital logic in bonds.
suggested_falsifier: Event study 2009-2021 daily: 5/10/20-day 6E drift conditional on ZN event-day sign vs matched non-event days, WITH a carry-neutralization control (residualize on front-back roll yield). Kill if drift vanishes under the carry control or lives in only one subsample (the Scholl-Uhlig critique realized).

name: Dealer-Inventory Overnight Drift (European-open window)
mechanism_class: Asymmetric risk premium — overnight equity premium concentration via dealer inventory risk
economic_actor_story: US-close market makers absorb one-sided customer imbalances (especially after selloffs) and carry unwanted inventory into the thin overnight session. They pay a concession to offload when the first deep liquidity pool arrives — the European open (~02:00-03:00 ET). The flow persists because end-of-day imbalance is mandated (funds must trade at/near close) and overnight risk-bearing capital is structurally thin; the loser is the closing-auction liquidity demander, the earner is whoever warehouses index risk from US close to European open.
representation: Hold long ES (or NQ) only inside fixed overnight clock windows, principally the European-open hour (02:00-04:00 ET) and secondarily 18:00-24:00 ET; condition size/direction on the prior US-day RTH return sign and close-hour imbalance proxy (last-30-min signed return / range). Published effect: drift is strongly positive after down days (overnight reversal), modest after up days.
markets: ES primary; NQ, RTY, YM confirmatory
data_needed: 1-min ES/NQ/RTY/YM 2022+ only; ET clock windows (mind DST — exchange-time vs London-time windows differ, a known program trap)
execution_realism: 1 RT/day at Globex-overnight spread; ES overnight is 1 tick ($12.50) wide so a ~2-4bp/hour drift can clear costs at ES notional; NQ overnight spread is wider and marginal — test on ES economics, execute where measured costs permit. Conditioning on down-days cuts trade count ~in half and roughly doubles per-trade edge per the published asymmetry.
evidence_source: Boyarchenko, Larsen, Whelan, 'The Overnight Drift', NY Fed Staff Report 917 (rev. 2022, RFS) — https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/staff_reports/sr917 ; Lou, Polk, Skouras 'A Tug of War: Overnight vs Intraday Expected Returns' (JFE 2019) for the broader overnight concentration fact
suggested_falsifier: Unconditional mean 1-min return by overnight clock-hour on ES 2022+, with circular-shift nulls preserving the diurnal grid; then the down-day-conditional table WITH its matched unconditional control in the same wave. Decisive and ~1 day of work. Kill if the European-open hour is not distinguishable from the overnight-hour distribution post-2022 (publication-decay is the live risk; sample is post-publication so this is a true out-of-sample read).

name: Cross-Sectional Skewness Premium in Futures (delta-1 skew premium)
mechanism_class: Asymmetric risk premium — skew preference priced in delta-1 futures, no options needed
economic_actor_story: Cumulative-prospect-theory investors overpay for lottery-like positive skew and overpay to avoid crash-like negative skew; commercial hedgers hedge selectively in the same direction. Holders of the most negatively-skewed contracts earn a premium as compensation for crash exposure; buyers of positive-skew 'lottery' contracts persistently overpay because the preference is behavioral, not informational, and hedger mandates do not respond to mispricing.
representation: Realized skewness of daily returns per root over trailing 12 months; rank across ~20 roots; long the most-negative-skew quintile, short the most-positive-skew quintile, rebalanced weekly/monthly. Must be orthogonalized against TSMOM and carry (curve slope) before quoting anything — overlap with existing factors is the null hypothesis.
markets: All ~20 daily roots (equity idx, GC/SI, CL, ZB/ZN, 6E); works as a cross-root portfolio, not per-instrument
horizon: Weekly to monthly rebalance, holding weeks
data_needed: Daily per-contract 2009+ on ~20 roots (already held); continuous-series construction from per-contract data (curve is computable, so roll-adjusted returns are buildable)
execution_realism: Turnover is low (rank changes slowly); at weekly rebalance, cost is a few RT per root per month — trivially survivable even at conservative all-in spreads. The binding constraint is breadth (20 roots is thin for a quintile sort; use terciles or signal-weighted).
evidence_source: Fernandez-Perez, Frijns, Fuertes, Miffre, 'The skewness of commodity futures returns', J. Banking & Finance 86 (2018) 143-158 — https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jbfina/v86y2018icp143-158.html ; related: Amaya-Christoffersen-Jacobs-Vasquez realized-skew in equities
suggested_falsifier: Rank-IC of trailing-12m skew vs next-month return across the 20 roots, 2009-2026, block-bootstrap null with shared draws per date (cross-sectional dependence preserved); then regress the L/S portfolio on TSMOM+carry factors built from the same roots. Kill if alpha t<2 after orthogonalization, or if the premium lives only pre-2015 (known factor-decay pattern).

name: Prior-Session Reference-Level Stop-Cascade / Anchoring Engine
mechanism_class: Behavioral underreaction — anchoring at prior settlement / prior-day high-low; stop-order clustering
economic_actor_story: Retail and discretionary traders anchor on yesterday's high/low/settlement: they place stops just beyond those levels and fade approaches to them ('it held before'). First touch of the level triggers clustered stops (a short-lived mechanical demand shock in the breakout direction), while anchored faders provide the other side and lose on genuine breaks. The flow persists because reference-level heuristics are the dominant retail/prop playbook and stop placement at visible levels is continuously replenished.
representation: Event = first RTH touch of prior-session RTH high (symmetrically low) after trading ≥N points away from it; measure the signed path 5-60 min post-touch, split by time-of-day and by gap context (open inside vs outside prior range). The tradeable claims are (a) short-horizon continuation immediately post-break (stop cascade) and (b) reversal when the touch occurs late-day or on the nth revisit.
markets: NQ, ES, RTY, YM (independent replications, one family); CL as out-of-family check
data_needed: 1-min bars 2022+ on the six 1-min roots; prior-session levels computed with the program's own 18:00-ET session boundary code
execution_realism: The hard gate: NQ RTH all-in is measured (~3 ticks/$15 spread + commission), so the conditional edge must exceed ~5-6 NQ ticks to survive — plausible for cascade moves (typically 15-40 ticks when they run) but the hit-rate does the work. ES cheaper per notional. 1-min bars cannot see the sub-minute cascade microstructure, only its 5-60 min residue — that residue is the only claim being tested.
evidence_source: George & Hwang 'The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing' (JF 2004) for anchoring-at-reference-highs; Osler 'Currency Orders and Exchange Rate Dynamics' (JF 2003) — direct evidence that stop-loss orders cluster just past round/reference levels and cause price cascades; ubiquitous practitioner literature (prior-day-high/low playbooks) is itself evidence the counterparty flow exists
suggested_falsifier: Class-conditional table (post-first-touch 30-min signed return by touch-type) against its matched unconditional control at identical time-of-day, circular-shift null; one wave on NQ+ES 2022-2026 pre-burn data. Kill if post-touch drift is inside the control band — this also kills claim (b) automatically since both come from the same event table.

name: Treasury Auction Concession Cycle (slow-moving dealer capital)
mechanism_class: Behavioral underreaction / limits-to-arbitrage — anticipated, repeated supply shocks not arbitraged
economic_actor_story: The US Treasury (the issuer) is the persistent loser: it pays a 9-18bp-of-auction-size concession because primary dealers must absorb duration at auctions with regulated, expensive balance sheet, and end-investor capital moves slowly. Prices cheapen for days into the auction and richen for days after — fully anticipated, published in advance, and still not arbed because the arbitrageur must warehouse exactly the duration risk dealers are being paid to take. Post-2015 evidence says compressed but not gone; 2022+ QT-era supply makes it worth re-measuring.
representation: Calendar-time event engine on ZB/ZN: short (or flat) duration D-3 to auction day of 10y/30y auctions, long auction-close to D+3. Auction dates/sizes are free public Treasury data (RAW-INFO novelty, $0 — allowed under 'no purchases'). Refinement: condition size on auction size vs trailing average (supply-shock intensity).
markets: ZB (30y auctions), ZN (10y); cross-check that ES shows nothing (specificity control)
data_needed: Daily ZB/ZN per-contract 2009+ (held) + free public auction calendar from treasurydirect.gov (no purchase); 1-min ZB 2022+ for intraday refinement of entry
execution_realism: Multi-day holding, 2 RT per event, ZB/ZN among the cheapest contracts on the board relative to daily vol — cost is a rounding error at this horizon. Capacity and slippage are non-issues. Main realism risk is signal size: if the modern concession is ~2-4bp, the per-event edge on 1 ZB is small in dollars; it is a portfolio-sleeve candidate, not a standalone book.
