evidence_source: Lou, Yan, Zhang, 'Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets', RFS 26(8) 2013 — https://ideas.repec.org/a/oup/rfinst/v26y2013i8p1891-1912.html ; follow-on work by Fleming & Liu (NY Fed) on intraday auction-cycle patterns; distinct from the program's killed macro-announcement direction cards — this is a SUPPLY-FLOW cycle, not an information event
suggested_falsifier: Event study of ZN/ZB returns D-5..D+5 around every 10y/30y auction 2009-2026 vs matched non-auction same-weekday days; shared-draw null across the auction family. Kill if the V-shape's post-2015 amplitude is statistically inside the control, or if it flips sign across the 2009-15 / 2016-21 / 2022+ eras (era stability is the second gate — the program's 3-era standard).

name: Correlation-Regime-Gated Flight-to-Quality (conditional tail engine)
mechanism_class: Tail/crisis engine with an OBSERVABLE regime gate — pays when long-equity books suffer, but only in the right macro regime
economic_actor_story: In growth-shock regimes, stressed equity holders (margin-called levered books, vol-targeting funds, mandate-bound de-riskers) buy Treasuries at any price during equity selloffs — they are forced, price-insensitive buyers, and whoever is already long duration collects. In inflation-shock regimes (2022) the same trade loses because bonds sell off WITH equities. The regime is directly observable in trailing realized ES-ZB correlation, so the engine's edge is refusing to pay the tail-hedge cost when the hedge is structurally broken.
representation: Gate: trailing 60-90d realized daily ES-ZB return correlation < 0 (regime ON). Trigger: ES intraday/1-day drawdown < -1.5σ of trailing vol. Action: long ZB for 1-5 days (or intraday from the equity-stress bar to next-day close). The card's claim is the INTERACTION: ZB's conditional return after equity stress is positive in the negative-correlation regime and ~zero/negative in the positive-correlation regime.
markets: ZB (execution leg), ES (trigger leg); NQ as alternative trigger
horizon: Event-driven, holding hours to 5 days; regime gate moves quarterly
data_needed: Daily ES/ZB 2009+ for the gate and the long-history event study; 1-min ES/ZB 2022+ for intraday trigger timing. All held. NOTE: distinct from MC-57 (ZB rates-state directional engine, NULL) — this is cross-asset, event-conditional, and only ever long ZB on equity stress
execution_realism: ZB spread is tight vs its daily range; ~2-6 events/quarter when gated, 2 RT each — cost-trivial. Real risk is regime-gate lag: correlation regimes flip over weeks (2022 flip took ~2 months to show in a 60d window), so the engine will eat the first stress events of every regime change. That lag cost must be inside the backtest, not assumed away.
evidence_source: Campbell, Pflueger, Viceira 'Macroeconomic Drivers of Bond and Equity Risks' (JPE 2020); Brixton, Brooks, Hecht, Ilmanen, Maloney, McQuinn 'A Changing Stock-Bond Correlation' (FAJ 2023); Baele, Bekaert, Inghelbrecht, Wei 'Flights to Safety' (RFS 2020); practitioner canon at AQR/PIMCO on the 2022 correlation flip
suggested_falsifier: 2x2 table: mean 1-day and 5-day ZB return after ES<-1.5σ days, split by corr-regime sign, 2009-2026, WITH the matched unconditional ZB mean in each regime as control (regime alone must not explain it). Shared-draw bootstrap across clustered stress events. Kill if the interaction term is not positive and distinguishable — the unconditional flight-to-quality fact without the gate is not the card.

name: Close-Window Mandated-Flow Momentum (LETF + dealer-gamma residue)
mechanism_class: Asymmetric risk premium — delta-1 expression of the intraday variance/gamma premium via end-of-day mandated rebalancing flow
economic_actor_story: Leveraged-ETF issuers MUST rebalance in the direction of the day's move into the close (a hard prospectus mandate, size ∝ daily return × AUM); short-gamma option dealers hedge the same direction on trend days. Both are price-insensitive, deadline-bound flows. The counterparty who provides that liquidity earns a premium; front-running the flow is the delta-1 way to be paid the dealers' short-gamma cost without touching options. Persists because the mandate cannot adapt — the issuer's tracking error, not P&L, is what it optimizes.
representation: Signal at 15:00-15:30 ET: sign and size of (a) day-so-far return from prior close and (b) first-half-hour return; position in that direction into 15:55-16:00 ET flatten. Trade only when |day-so-far return| > threshold (the flow is convex in the move: on flat days there is no rebalance to front-run). Published amplification on high-vol/high-volume/macro days is the size filter.
markets: NQ (TQQQ/SQQQ complex is the largest LETF pool relative to underlying), ES, RTY (TNA/TZA)
horizon: 25-55 minutes, once daily, conditional (~30-40% of days after filter)
data_needed: 1-min NQ/ES/RTY 2022+ (held); measured NQ RTH cost model (held). No options or flow data needed — the day's return IS the flow proxy
execution_realism: Best-costed slot in the whole card set: RTH close liquidity is the day's deepest, NQ cost measured at ~3 ticks all-in, and the filter concentrates trades on big-range days where the last-half-hour move averages many times cost. 1 RT/day max. Known decay risk: the raw first-half-hour→last-half-hour effect weakened post-2018 in US large-cap; the conditional (big-move, high-vol) version is the live claim.
evidence_source: Gao, Han, Li, Zhou 'Market Intraday Momentum', JFE 129 (2018) — https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v129y2018i2p394-414.html ; Cheng & Madhavan 'The Dynamics of Leveraged and Inverse ETFs' (2009) for the mandated-rebalance arithmetic; Bogousslavsky (2016) infrequent-rebalancing theory; Baltas & Kosowski on futures intraday patterns
suggested_falsifier: Regress last-30-min return on day-so-far return, NQ/ES 2022-2026, unconditionally and above the |move| threshold, with time-of-day-preserving circular-shift null; check the program's prior clock-bucket-periodicity kill (that was P1-conditional — the unconditional close-window regression was not the object killed). Kill if conditional beta ≤ 0 or if edge < measured all-in cost at the stated trade rate.

name: Panic-State Momentum Router (bear+vol two-state gate)
mechanism_class: State-space/regime model with observable indicators — routing between continuation and reversal policy by panic state
economic_actor_story: Momentum is a crowded convergence trade in calm states (underreaction dominates, continuation pays); in panic states — market below trailing 12-24m mean AND realized vol elevated — the momentum crowd is capital-constrained and unwinds together, so past losers rebound violently and continuation-followers are the losers. The persistence is structural: most systematic momentum capital cannot flip its policy by state (mandates, lookback rigidity), so the state-conditional wrongness of the crowd is durable. The router's edge is POLICY novelty, not new information.
representation: Observable state: (bear = continuous-series trailing 12m return < 0) x (RV regime = 20d realized vol / 250d realized vol > threshold). Policy: in state CALM run continuation (weekly TSMOM sign per root); in state PANIC cut gross and/or flip the losers-leg to reversal for 1-4 week horizon. The card's testable content is the INTERACTION — continuation profitability as a function of state — not the base TSMOM (which alone would be a banned generic entry).
markets: ES/RTY/YM/GC/CL/ZB daily complex (the ~20 roots); explicitly NOT NQ (P1's turf; also NQ is the program's measured momentum outlier)
horizon: Positions held days-weeks; state variable moves monthly
data_needed: Daily per-contract 2009+ (held); realized vol and 12m return computable from held data; no external state variable needed (VIX not required — 20d/250d RV ratio is the observable)
execution_realism: Weekly rebalance across liquid roots — cost-trivial. The realism risk is statistical, not executional: panic states are rare (~15-20% of months), so the interaction test has maybe 30-40 independent panic months in 2009-2026; power must be computed BEFORE running (the program's N-bound discipline) — if the design cannot reach power at the documented effect size (Daniel-Moskowitz: dynamic version ~doubles Sharpe), park it rather than run it underpowered.
evidence_source: Daniel & Moskowitz 'Momentum Crashes', JFE 122 (2016) — https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jfinec/v122y2016i2p221-247.html ; Cooper, Gutierrez, Hameed 'Market States and Momentum' (JF 2004); Barroso & Santa-Clara 'Momentum has its moments' (JFE 2015) for the vol-scaled variant
suggested_falsifier: Pooled regression of next-month continuation-portfolio return on the panic-state dummy across the non-NQ roots, shared-draw null per month (cross-root dependence preserved), 2009-2026. Power calc first. Kill if the state interaction is ≤ 0 or underpowered-by-design; do NOT promote the CALM-state TSMOM leg alone under any outcome (that would be the banned generic card wearing a costume).

name: Nearness-to-Rolling-High Anchoring (52-week-high underreaction in futures)
mechanism_class: Behavioral underreaction — anchoring on salient reference price causes slow incorporation of news
economic_actor_story: Traders anchor on the rolling 52-week high as 'too expensive to buy': when good news pushes price near the reference high, anchored holders sell early (disposition) and anchored buyers wait for pullbacks, so the news is under-incorporated and price drifts up for weeks after. Symmetrically near 52-week lows. The loser is the anchored trader who systematically fades strength near reference extremes; the heuristic is hard-wired and replenished by each cohort. Distinct from TSMOM: the signal is LEVEL relative to a reference extreme, not past return — the two disagree materially after V-shaped paths.
representation: Per root: nearness = current price / trailing 252d high (continuous series, roll-adjusted). Cross-sectional: long high-nearness, short low-nearness across ~20 roots, monthly. Time-series variant per instrument: long when nearness > 0.95, with weekly refresh. Must report correlation to and residual alpha over plain 12m TSMOM on the same roots — the anchoring claim IS the residual.
markets: The ~20 daily roots cross-sectionally; ES/CL/GC time-series variants
data_needed: Daily per-contract 2009+ (held); roll-adjusted continuous series construction (curve data held). Nothing external
execution_realism: Monthly turnover across deep contracts — negligible cost at any plausible spread model. The realism question is crowding/decay: the equity version is public since 2004; the futures cross-sectional version is less arbed (documented separately in commodities). Survival post-2015 is the real test, and the held data covers it.
evidence_source: George & Hwang 'The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing', JF 59(5) 2004; Bianchi-Drew-Fan and related work applying 52-week-high momentum to commodity futures (documented positive premium distinct from conventional momentum); Baker, Pan, Wurgler 'Anchoring on Credible Anchors' (JFE 2012) for the anchoring mechanism in reference prices
suggested_falsifier: Cross-root rank-IC of nearness vs next-month return, 2009-2026, monthly shared-draw bootstrap; then residual alpha after regressing the nearness L/S on the TSMOM L/S from the same roots. Kill if residual alpha t<2 or if the effect is entirely subsumed by TSMOM — subsumption is the single most likely failure mode and the test is one afternoon on held daily data.

name: Signal-bar spread capture (passive-entry policy with timeout fallback)
mechanism_class: execution alpha / passive-vs-aggressive policy
economic_actor_story: P1 pays the taker's half-spread plus impact on every entry. The market maker's quoted spread prices adverse selection against genuinely informed short-horizon flow — but a multi-hour momentum signal is nearly uninformed at the seconds horizon, so the MM systematically over-charges P1's actual toxicity. That surplus is recoverable by posting. It persists because most retail/CTA flow defaults to market orders for certainty-of-fill, keeping the quoted spread wide enough to pay passive providers.
representation: At signal-bar close, place a join-the-bid limit (long-only book); escalate to market after T seconds or after k-tick runaway. Measure fill rate, post-fill adverse drift, and realized entry vs the current market-order baseline, per entry.
markets: NQ/MNQ first (only root with measured costs + BBO sample); policy is portable to any future engine.
horizon: seconds-to-minutes execution overlay on multi-hour holds
data_needed: In-house only: P1 historical signal timestamps, archived NQ BBO sample, measured NQ cost model (COST_MODEL.md). Nothing new.
execution_realism: Prize is up to ~1 spread per entry (measured NQ RTH spread ~3 ticks = $15/RT); this is a direct cost-line subtraction, not a new risk position. The bounding risk is non-fill concentrated on exactly the strongest-momentum entries (reverse adverse selection).
evidence_source: Frazzini, Israel & Moskowitz, 'Trading Costs' (JF 2018) — patient/limit execution realizes a fraction of demanded-liquidity cost estimates; Almgren & Chriss optimal-execution framework; Baron, Brogaard, Hagströmer & Kirilenko (JFQA 2019) on aggressor costs in futures; Glosten–Milgrom logic for why an uninformed-at-short-horizon taker overpays.
suggested_falsifier: Pure replay, no new signal research: run P1's historical entries against the archived BBO with limit-at-join + T-sec timeout. Policy is dead if fill-weighted price improvement minus alpha foregone on unfilled/late entries (computed from the realized P&L of those same trades) <= 0 across T in {5s,30s,120s}.

name: Liquidity-state-aware entry deferral (time-of-day cost curve routing)
mechanism_class: execution alpha / spread-state-aware timing policy
economic_actor_story: CME equity-futures liquidity has a strong deterministic intraday cycle (thin overnight, around cash open/close and scheduled releases; deep mid-RTH). Any strategy whose signal clock is set independently of the liquidity clock donates the state-dependent extra spread to market makers who widen predictably. Persists because signal engines almost never co-optimize their execution clock.
representation: Build an hour-of-day + event-window-flag (8:30/10:00/10:30/14:00 releases) expected-cost curve from the NQ BBO sample. Policy: when a signal fires in a high-cost state, defer execution up to X minutes into the next low-cost state, X bounded by the signal's measured alpha-decay curve.
markets: NQ/MNQ now; curve shape re-estimated per root later.
data_needed: NQ BBO sample, measured cost model, P1 trade history. Nothing new.
execution_realism: Only re-times by minutes, so the binding quantity is momentum alpha decay over the deferral window — directly measurable in-sample on P1's own trades. Savings are the wide-state minus tight-state spread differential.
evidence_source: Intraday spread periodicity: McInish & Wood (JF 1992, equities U-shape); CME Group's own liquidity research notes on ES/NQ intraday liquidity profiles; standard sell-side TCA practice (time-of-day cost curves are ubiquitous at futures desks); Almgren-style cost scheduling.
suggested_falsifier: Two-column replay over historical signals: actual clock vs deferred clock. Dead if cost saved < alpha lost, with alpha decay measured on the same trade set; also dead if the intraday cost curve is flat within noise in the BBO sample.

name: Micro-vs-full notional routing (MNQ vs NQ all-in cost crossover)
mechanism_class: execution alpha / micro-vs-full contract routing policy
economic_actor_story: Arbitrageurs keep micro and E-mini locked in price, but the quoted spread in points and commission per notional differ and move independently: retail-dominated MNQ top-of-book can be tighter in points while its commission per notional is ~3x worse. Habitual routing (always-mini or always-micro) pays the wrong all-in rate whenever the state flips. Two in-house live samples already show MNQ tighter than NQ at those instants.
representation: Per-entry choice between 1 NQ and notional-equivalent MNQ (or a split), decided by spread-state estimate: time-of-day prior plus the paired front/back NQ+MNQ GetQuote samples from the quarterly crossover-sampling programme. All-in $/notional = spread_pts x multiplier + commission per route.
markets: NQ vs MNQ (live-relevant: the 2047681 book already executes in MNQ).
data_needed: Commission templates (Lifetime $4.36/ctrRT NQ; micro template in NT8), live MNQ fills, the 4-hourly roll-window quote sampling already running. MNQ historical quotes do not exist in-house — the card is built on the sampling programme, not on backfill.
execution_realism: Bounded, small, but pure cost reduction with zero position risk. At small size the crossover is plausible precisely because MNQ commission/notional penalty (~3x) can be smaller than the spread differential in thin states; in deep RTH the NQ route should dominate.
evidence_source: CME Group micro E-mini liquidity/adoption notes (micro vs mini spread comparisons); practitioner TCA on micro futures. No academic canon — this is a measured-in-house mechanism, and the in-house n=2 is the only direct evidence so far.
suggested_falsifier: The already-scheduled paired quote samples: compute all-in $/notional for both routes at each sample. Mechanism dead if the NQ route dominates in >=95% of sampled states; alive if MNQ wins in an identifiable state (e.g., overnight) often enough to matter at P1's trade frequency.

name: EIA-Wednesday post-release price-discovery continuation in CL
mechanism_class: commodity-native / scheduled-release gradual information diffusion
economic_actor_story: The 10:30 ET Weekly Petroleum Status Report resolves a material supply datum. Machine readers trade the print in seconds, but full incorporation involves slower same-direction flow over the next 15-90 minutes: commercial hedgers re-quoting programs, discretionary energy traders, dealers re-hedging. The loser is the fader who treats the initial spike as noise and the slow institution that pays worse prices later. Persists because the slow flow is mandate-driven, not price-driven. Crucially, direction is read off the tape itself — no consensus/surprise vendor data needed, which routes around the program's N-bound veto on buying surprise data.
representation: On EIA report days (deterministic calendar: Wed 10:30 ET; Thu after Monday holidays), sign of CL return over 10:30-10:35 -> hold same direction 30-90 min, entering ~10:33-10:35 after the spread normalizes. Mandatory matched unconditional control: identical clock window on non-report days, same wave (per house rules).
markets: CL
horizon: 30-90 minutes, ~48 events/yr (~230 events on 2022-mid-2026 pre-seal data)
data_needed: CL 1-min 2022+ (in-house) + the deterministic public release calendar. Nothing purchasable.
execution_realism: CL RT friction ~$10-20 vs typical post-EIA 1-hr ranges of many tens of ticks; survivable if the conditional mean is even a modest fraction of the event range. Entry must avoid the 10:30:00-10:32 wide-spread window.
evidence_source: Ederington & Lee (JF 1993) on announcement resolution; Bjursell, Gentle & Wang on jumps/volume around EIA releases in energy futures; Elder, Miao & Ramchander (2013) on intraday crude price discovery; Halova/Kurov-line work on energy inventory news. Practitioner lore is split ('EIA head-fake' reversal vs continuation) — the falsifier decides the sign. Note: the house's own macro-release finding (powered vol / no direction) tested unconditional direction; this is tape-conditioned direction, a different event definition.
suggested_falsifier: One preregistered table: tape-conditioned continuation vs matched non-event control, circular-shift null preserving dependence, era-split 2022/23/24/25. Dead if conditional mean is indistinguishable from control or the sign flips across eras.

name: Commodity-index roll congestion in CL calendar spreads (Goldman-roll pressure)
mechanism_class: commodity-native / predictable price-insensitive flow (index roll mechanics)
economic_actor_story: Passive commodity-index capital (GSCI/BCOM trackers) must sell front CL and buy the deferred on a published fixed schedule (GSCI: 5th-9th business day). The flow is date-certain, size-large, and price-insensitive; liquidity providers demand payment, so the front-vs-second spread predictably weakens into/through the roll window and reverts after. The loser is the index investor who accepts schedule certainty over execution price — a mandate choice that persists by construction. Known decay after ~2010-2015 as roll timing diversified; the decay itself is cheap to measure and closes the card if fatal.
representation: Daily per-contract CL 2009+ -> front/second calendar-spread return in event time by business-day-of-month; position = short the pressured side during business days ~4-9, or trade the post-window mean reversion. Outright-front residual variant as secondary.
markets: CL (extendable to other index-heavy roots in the daily panel later)
data_needed: Daily per-contract 2009+ (explicitly available; the curve is computable). Nothing new.
execution_realism: Calendar-spread moves are small; commission x2 legs (~$8.72 RT at Lifetime) plus two spreads is the hurdle, and live spread execution is not yet built in NT8 — research-first card. The 2009-2026 panel decides whether post-2015 magnitude survives friction before any execution work is spent.
evidence_source: Mou (2011 working paper, 'Limits to Arbitrage and Commodity Index Investment' — front-running the Goldman roll); Bessembinder, Carrion, Tuttle & Venkataraman (JFE 2016) on liquidity around predictable index trades; Irwin/Sanders-line work documenting roll-impact decay.
suggested_falsifier: Event-time panel of spread returns by business-day-of-month, 2009-2026, split into thirds. Dead if the post-2015 window mean is inside the friction band or sign-flipped — one table, no execution build required.

name: Treasury auction-cycle concession and post-auction rebound in ZB/ZN
mechanism_class: rates-native / dealer balance-sheet supply cycle
economic_actor_story: Primary dealers must absorb known, repeated, date-certain duration supply at note/bond auctions. Limited dealer risk capacity cheapens the secondary market into the auction (concession) and richens it during post-auction distribution — a recurring payment from a deliberately price-insensitive issuer (Treasury) and from investors unwilling to pre-position, to balance-sheet providers. Persists because dealer VaR constraints persist; documented across decades and countries.
representation: Daily ZB/ZN 2009+ returns in event time around the rule-based monthly auction schedule (mid-month refunding cluster for 10y/30y, reconstructible from Treasury's regular pattern — no data purchase). Long duration auction-day close to +3/+5 days; flat/short in the -3..0 concession window. Intraday secondary variant: ZB 1-min around the 13:00 ET result on auction days (2022+).
markets: ZB, ZN
data_needed: Daily 2009+ on ZB/ZN (in the ~20-root panel), ZB 1-min 2022+, deterministic public auction calendar. Nothing new.
execution_realism: The most cost-robust card here: multi-day hold in half-tick/1-32nd markets makes friction a rounding error; the entire question is whether the post-publication (Lou-Yan-Zhang 2013) magnitude survives in 2015+ data.
evidence_source: Lou, Yan & Zhang (RFS 2013, 'Anticipated and Repeated Shocks in Liquid Markets') — recurring ~10bp-order concession/rebound cycles around 10y auctions; NY Fed work on dealer inventory around auctions (Fleming and coauthors); Sigaux on pre-auction price dynamics; Beetsma et al. on the same cycle in eurozone auctions. Note: house MC-57 was a rates-STATE card and its null does not touch this supply-cycle event definition.
suggested_falsifier: Event-time daily panel 2009-2026 by auction type with matched non-auction control weeks and era-split thirds. Dead if the post-2015 rebound is <= 0 net of friction; the intraday variant is only opened if the daily cycle survives.

name: FOMC press-conference verbal price-discovery drift
mechanism_class: rates-native / Fed-communication microstructure (sequential information release)
economic_actor_story: The 14:00 ET statement is machine-read instantly, but the 14:30 press conference releases information sequentially over ~45 minutes, and most institutional capital will not trade mid-conference (headline risk, mandates) — so prices drift during the conference in the direction the tape has already revealed, with the waiting institutions as the late-paying counterparty. Persists because the abstention is policy-driven, not ignorance-driven.
representation: No NLP at $0: sign of the 14:00-14:30 statement-window return in ZB (and ES/NQ) on FOMC days -> hold same direction 14:30-15:30 through the conference. Enter at ~14:28-14:30 after statement-window spreads normalize. Matched non-FOMC 14:30-15:30 control in the same wave.
markets: ZB primary; ES/NQ secondary
horizon: 1 hour, 8 events/yr (~36 events on 2022-mid-2026 pre-seal data) — explicitly the weakest-powered card in this set
data_needed: ZB + ES/NQ 1-min 2022+, deterministic FOMC calendar. Nothing new.
execution_realism: 1-hour RTH hold in deep markets on the year's most liquid afternoons; friction trivial relative to FOMC-day ranges (house MC-55 already measured RV expanding x5.66 post-FOMC — the vol is real and powered; the open question is tape-conditioned direction, which MC-55 did not test).
evidence_source: Gómez-Cram & Grotteria (RFS 2022, 'Real-Time Price Discovery via Verbal Communication') — drift during press conferences in the direction of revealed tone; Lucca & Moench (JF 2015) pre-FOMC drift as the cautionary precedent (largely decayed post-publication).
suggested_falsifier: 36-event preregistered sign test + continuation regression vs matched control, with the honest admission that only a large effect can clear at this N: kill immediately if in-sample t < 1. Cheapest decisive test in the group — one afternoon of compute.

name: Month-end London 4pm fix equity-hedge rebalancing in 6E
mechanism_class: FX-native / benchmark-fix rebalancing flow
economic_actor_story: Cross-border institutional equity holders hedge FX at the WM/R 4pm London fix, and month-end rebalancing flow is mechanically predictable from the month's relative equity performance: US equities up implies foreign holders must sell USD at the fix to restore hedge ratios. The flow is benchmark-driven and price-insensitive (fix trackers are judged against the fix, not against cost); dealers pre-hedge, moving price into the fix with partial reversal after. The loser is the mandate-bound hedger; the mandate persists even after the 2015 fix-window reform.
representation: Built deliberately to survive having no intraday 6E data: daily 6E 2009+ (in the ~20-root panel) month-end-day return signed by the month-to-date ES return (hedge-rebalancing proxy) — expect 6E up (USD selling) into month-end when US equities outperformed, concentrated in top-tercile signal months; plus a next-1-3-day partial-reversal leg.
markets: 6E (extendable to other FX roots in the daily panel)
data_needed: Daily per-contract 6E + daily ES, both 2009+. Nothing new; no intraday FX data required by construction.
execution_realism: Daily-horizon 6E friction is small (~1-2 pips equivalent); documented effect sizes are tens of bps on strong-signal month-ends, so survivability hinges on conditioning to top-tercile months rather than trading every month-end.
evidence_source: Melvin & Prins (2015, 'Equity hedging and exchange rates at the London 4pm fix'); Evans on fix-window price dynamics; BIS work (Krohn & Sushko) on dealer pre-hedging at the fix; FSB/BIS WM/R reform reports for the 2015 regime break.
suggested_falsifier: 2009-2026 daily panel: month-end 6E return regressed on the month's equity-performance signal, plus the reversal leg, era-split across the 2015 fix-window reform. Dead if the post-2015 slope is ~0 or the effect lives only pre-reform.
